models.name: detector
models.source: Ultralytics YOLOv8m pretrained on full 80-class COCO (stock, not fine-tuned), dynamically INT8-quantized with onnxruntime.quantization.quantize_dynamic (QUInt8 weights) on 2026-11-14 to recover real-time speed. Tried in order on this repo's dev machine (desktop CPU, onnxruntime, 640x640): yolov8n ~31ms/frame (COCO mAP50-95 37.3) -> yolov8s ~90ms (44.9) -> yolov8m fp32 ~230ms (50.2, rejected: too slow for a real-time hazard alert) -> yolov8l fp32 ~478ms (52.9, clearly unusable) -> yolov8m INT8 ~108ms (kept: m's higher accuracy at near-yolov8s speed). Post-quantization spot check on a real COCO image showed every class's detection confidence matching or exceeding yolov8s's own (chair 0.89 vs 0.84, dining table 0.76 vs 0.58, refrigerator 0.71 vs 0.50, clock 0.58 vs 0.47). An own-data fine-tune (yolov8s_general.onnx, now at computer_vision/training/exported_previous/yolov8s_general_from_scratch.onnx) was tried first and rejected: its 150-images-per-class COCO subsample starved 'bench'/'chair' (held-out recall 0.05 / 0.18), worse than any stock checkpoint. Vehicle body types (bicycle/car/motorcycle/bus/truck) are merged into one 'transportation' display class entirely in software (DetectorConfig.classMap / YoloDecoder), at zero accuracy cost to the other 75 COCO classes. Note: 'bench' and 'chair' remain structurally low-AP categories across essentially all public object detectors (COCO leaderboards), not specific to this app -- no model swap reaches 80%+ on them. NOT YET VERIFIED: on-device (phone/NNAPI) latency, and whether onnxruntime-android's kernel set covers this quantization's ops -- only desktop CPU with the desktop onnxruntime package has been checked.
models.input: [1,3,640,640] float32 RGB, letterboxed and normalized to [0,1]
models.output: [1,84,8400] float32: xywh plus 80 COCO class scores
models.labels: COCO 80 labels; app filters + remaps (bicycle/car/motorcycle/bus/truck -> transportation) using android/app/src/main/resources/config/detector.json

models.name: detector-pothole
models.license: AGPL-3.0 (Ultralytics YOLOv8 derivative; no separate license stated on the model card)
models.source: Pretrained single-class pothole detector from Hugging Face (keremberke/yolov8n-pothole-segmentation), trained by its author on keremberke/pothole-segmentation (CC BY 4.0 -- the same dataset already documented at datasets/data/detection/public_sources/hf_pothole_keremberke/SOURCE.md). A segmentation checkpoint; exported to ONNX with ultralytics 8.4.172, imgsz=640, opset=12. Added 2026-11-14 to replace the general model's own pothole class, which only ever had 90 generic stock photos to learn from (recall 0.696) -- this dedicated model's own reported box mAP50 is 0.858 on its validation split (third-party listing; not independently re-verified against Egyptian roads, which neither model has seen).
models.input: [1,3,640,640] float32 RGB, letterboxed and normalized to [0,1]
models.output: [1,37,8400] float32: xywh plus 1 pothole class score plus 32 mask coefficients (segmentation export) -- the app's decoder only reads rows 4..5 and ignores the 32 mask rows, see YoloDecoder.kt.

models.name: detector-general-finetune-superseded
models.source: Superseded on 2026-11-14 by the stock yolov8n_coco_stock.onnx + classMap approach above (better per-class accuracy, no fine-tuning needed for classes COCO already covers). Kept only as a reference/rollback artifact, not built into the app. Held-out test mAP50-95 was 0.387 (person 0.515 recall, transportation 0.565, bench 0.050, chair 0.180, fire hydrant 0.777, stop sign 0.800, parking meter 0.435) -- see computer_vision/training/train_yolo_colab.ipynb.
models.input: [1,3,640,640] float32 RGB, letterboxed and normalized to [0,1]
models.output: [1,12,8400] float32: xywh plus 8 class scores (person, transportation, pothole, bench, chair, fire hydrant, stop sign, parking meter)

models.name: detector-stock-coco80-backup
models.source: Identical bytes to the shipped 'detector' entry above -- kept as a rollback copy outside android/app/src/main/assets/ (see models/stock_coco80_backup/detector.json for its original, pre-classMap config shape).
models.input: [1,3,640,640] float32 RGB, letterboxed and normalized to [0,1]
models.output: [1,84,8400] float32: xywh plus 80 COCO class scores
